run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:24:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504 responses on the frontend-proxy 'ingress' operation. Those spans last about 15.0 s, matching the proxy's own upstream timeout: in trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20 the frontend's POST /api/checkout (15.72 s) is blocked inside checkout's 'orders publish' span (15.58 s) while every other span in that same trace (cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote, payment, email, flagd, ad) completes in microseconds to about 91 ms. checkout's Kafka produce was sub-millisecond until 14:21:28 (logged durations of 182.789, 261.656 and similar microseconds), then the kafka Deployment was rollout-restarted at 14:21:34 (new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485, old pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 deleted at 14:21:36, identical image, restartedAt annotation). checkout then logged connection refused to kafka:9092 and circuit-breaker-open produce failures between 14:21:42 and 14:23:16, the new broker only logged 'Kafka Server started' at 14:23:11 although its pod had been Ready since 14:21:36 (the template defines no readiness probe), and by 14:30-14:31 produces only succeeded after 11.4-19.2 s. That latency pushes checkout past the proxy's 15 s timeout, so the alert fires on frontend-proxy while the fault originates in the restarted kafka Deployment. Affected, each on its own evidence: frontend-proxy (its own 504 error spans), checkout (its own failed produce log lines and 15 s 'orders publish' spans), load-generator (its own 504 span in the sampled trace), and the kafka Deployment as origin. Checked and not failing on their own signals: the frontend service (zero error spans, all non-checkout operations p90 at or below 193 ms), the frontend-proxy and checkout pods (restartCount 0, Ready), and accounting consumer spans (p90 stable near 91 ms).

claims.text: frontend-proxy span metrics show errors only on the 'ingress' operation: over the 12 minutes ending 14:36:45 the error increase was 188.47 spans on ingress and 0 on 'router frontend egress', with 5446.59 and 5635.06 spans having no status respectively. These are span counts, not request counts.

frontend-proxy ingress error spans were near baseline before the incident (4 per 2 min at 14:20:45, 0 at 14:22:45) and then sustained at 27.81, 25.33, 32.0, 21.51, 21.33 and 26.35 per 2-minute window from 14:24:45 through 14:34:45, against 738-967 non-error ingress spans per window.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 with otel.status_code ERROR and durations near 15.0 s (15001259 us, 15001177 us and similar), and their paired 'router frontend egress' spans carry error true with http.status_code 0 and the same near-15.0 s duration; this pattern repeats across the first 40 rows of the matching error spans.

Trace d3066bd6d4294c09a9c14e1f7b11fd20 shows the full path: load-generator POST 15.00 s with http.status_code 504 and error true, frontend-proxy ingress 15.00 s with http.status_code 504 and otel.status_code ERROR, router frontend egress 15.00 s with error true and http.status_code 0, frontend POST /api/checkout 15.72 s and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 15.72 s (both http.status_code 200), checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 15.72 s, checkout orders publish 15.58 s, while cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping, quote, payment, email, flagd and ad spans in the same trace take 5 us to 91 ms.

frontend service span metrics at 14:36:45 are slow only on the checkout path: p90 is 15000 ms for POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and POST, while every other frontend operation has p90 between 48.7 ms and 193.3 ms.
checkout orders publish p90 was 1.8 ms at every sample from 14:01:45 to 14:22:45 and then 15000 ms at 14:25:45, 14:28:45, 14:31:45 and 14:34:45.

checkout logs between 14:21:42 and 14:23:16 repeatedly show failed connects to broker kafka:9092 (dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092 connect connection refused), client metadata errors from broker -1, failed produce to topic orders with circuit breaker is open, and standalone circuit breaker is open messages.

Before the kafka rollout checkout produce calls succeeded in sub-millisecond time: log lines at 14:20:55-14:21:28 report successful write with durations of 182.789, 137.261, 172.646, 142.905, 197.104, 146.389, 136.501, 181.793, 141.403, 162.266, 157.024, 132.456, 124.577, 135.896, 213.785, 133.028, 163.553, 239.863, 149.82 and 261.656 microseconds.

Kubernetes events tie the kafka change to a controller rollout: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet scaled kafka-5c9d7cc485 from 0 to 1 at 14:21:34 and scaled kafka-ff7884766 from 1 to 0 at 14:21:36, ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 recorded SuccessfulCreate at 14:21:34, pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 was killed and ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 recorded SuccessfulDelete at 14:21:36, and pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 was scheduled at 14:21:34 with container Started at 14:21:35.

The kafka Deployment now has ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 created 2026-11-16T14:21:34Z with 1 ready replica, while the previous ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 created 2026-11-16T13:48:29Z holds 0 replicas; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka.

The two kafka ReplicaSet pod templates are otherwise identical, the new one carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt 2026-11-16T14:21:34Z, neither template defines volumes, and the kafka container has no readinessProbe or livenessProbe.

Pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 is Running and Ready (Ready condition lastTransitionTime 2026-11-16T14:21:36Z) with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, its kafka container started at 14:21:35Z, and it is owned by ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485.

The new kafka broker was still starting well after its pod was Ready: it logged finishing the wait for SocketServer acceptors at 14:23:05, BrokerServer transition from STARTING to STARTED and Kafka Server started at 14:23:11.

The restarted broker rebuilt its state: kafka logs at 14:23:14-14:23:15 show creation of all __consumer_offsets partitions, an auto-creation request for topic orders answered with TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS, creation of new partition orders-0 with topic id jFTsf7SeQ1qWRVM3q-fI-A, and partition orders-0 loaded with initial high watermark 0.
Deployment kafka is at revision 2 with replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, and condition NewReplicaSetAvailable with lastUpdateTime 2026-11-16T14:21:36Z.

kafka is the only otel-demo workload whose pod is younger than the incident: every other pod listed started between 13:48:29Z and 13:50:15Z with restartCount 0 (fraud-detection shows 2), while kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 started 14:21:34Z.
The kafka Service Endpoints currently target the new pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 at IP 100.96.4.3 on ports 9092 (plaintext) and 9093 (controller).

In the 10 minutes ending 14:36:45 the error-span increase is 0 for accounting, ad, checkout orders publish, all listed frontend operations (including POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and payment; the only nonzero entries are frontend-proxy ingress at 157.14 and recommendation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at 1.07.

checkout recorded 16.31 error spans in the 5 minutes ending 14:26:45 and 0 in the 5-minute buckets ending 14:31:45 and 14:36:45, while frontend-proxy 5-minute error counts rose to 61.11, 95.56 and 55.43 at 14:26:45, 14:31:45 and 14:36:45 versus 2.36, 0, 5.56, 5.56 and 7.78 earlier.
accounting consumer-side latency did not escalate: p90 stayed at 90.71-92.36 ms for orders receive, 1.81-1.87 ms for otel and 4035-4672 ms for order-consumed across 14:00:45-14:35:45.

Primary hypothesis: the kafka Deployment restart at 14:21:34 is the origin of the frontend-proxy 504s. It replaced the only broker, which stayed unavailable until Kafka Server started at 14:23:11 and produced checkout connection-refused and circuit-breaker failures, and afterwards produce acknowledgements took 11-19 s, pushing checkout PlaceOrder past frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout so the proxy returned 504.

Second hypothesis for the multi-second acknowledgements: because the pod template mounts no volume and Kafka writes under /tmp/kafka-logs, replacing the pod discarded the broker log and the restarted broker had to recreate __consumer_offsets and orders-0 with initial high watermark 0 at 14:23:15; that rebuilt state plausibly contributes to the slow produce responses, though no broker-internal timing metric proves it.

The kafka Deployment has no readiness probe, so the new pod was marked Ready at 14:21:36 while the broker only listened from 14:23:11; requests should therefore have been routed to a non-listening broker for roughly 1.5 minutes, which lines up with checkout connection-refused logs from 14:21:42 to 14:23:16 and with the first sustained 504 window measured at 14:24:45.

Alternative client-side explanation of the 11-19 s produce durations: checkout's Kafka client may be retrying after the outage and circuit-breaker trip, so the logged figure may include retry backoff rather than pure broker processing; the log records total produce duration only, so the split between broker slowness and client retry is undetermined.

Broker resource pressure could also contribute: the kafka container is limited to cpu 400m and memory 900Mi with KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS -Xmx400M -Xms400M; no container CPU throttling or memory series were available in this Run, so this remains unverified.

Rejected: frontend-proxy is itself the faulty component. Its pod has restartCount 0 and is Ready, its router frontend egress error-span increase is 0, and its ingress 504s carry about 15.0 s duration matching an upstream timeout while the frontend span for the same request finished with http.status_code 200 after 15.72 s, so the proxy surfaces the timeout rather than originating it.

Rejected: the frontend service is failing on its own. Its error-span increase is 0 for every listed frontend operation in the 10 minutes ending 14:36:45, and its p90 reaches 15000 ms only on the checkout path while all other operations are 48.7-193.3 ms.

Rejected: kafka was damaged by a crash, OOM or eviction rather than rolled out. The new pod shows restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, its events are controller-driven SuccessfulCreate and SuccessfulDelete plus Deployment ScalingReplicaSet at 14:21:34 and 14:21:36, and no Evicted or OOMKilled event appeared for kafka.

Not every frontend-proxy error is explained by the kafka restart: small ingress error counts already existed before it (4 per 2 min at 14:20:45 and 1.33-4 per 2 min at several points from 14:00:45 onward, against 0 at 14:22:45), so a low-rate error source predates the kafka change.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule could not be inspected because the list_prometheus_rules query for rule name RequestErrorRate returned status no_data, so the alert expression and the reported value 0.4 are unverified and the span-based error counts cited here are not a request error rate.

A Jaeger search for frontend-proxy spans tagged error=true in 13:56:00-13:58:00 returned status no_data, so the small pre-existing frontend-proxy errors before 14:21 have no established HTTP status or cause and are not attributed to this incident.

Kafka and checkout container logs end at 14:31:03 and 14:31:15 (log read-through limits), so the final minutes before this report are unknown from logs, and the deleted pre-restart kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 left no readable previous-container logs.
A checkout log query restricted to 14:24:00-14:36:45 with an error filter returned status no_data, so it cannot be asserted as fact that checkout logged no further failures after 14:23:16.

Several log views used here are limit-truncated (kafka and checkout log fetches, checkout error fetch, accounting fetch) and the frontend-proxy error-span view is a truncated read slice of 980 rows, so unseen lines and rows remain unknown.

No container CPU, memory or throttling series for the kafka pod were available, so the mechanism behind the 11-19 s produce acknowledgements (broker slowness versus client retries versus resource limits) cannot be confirmed.
Jaeger retains only recent traces and the trace and metric views are sampled, so services and operations not returned by these queries are unknown rather than proven error-free.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so there is no deployment or change audit trail beyond the Kubernetes objects and events observed.
next_steps: Inspect the actual RequestErrorRate rule and the metric and labels it divides, to reconcile the reported 0.4 and to confirm whether the threshold reacts to the pre-existing low-rate errors.

Confirm the broker's post-restart produce latency from Kafka request and produce latency metrics plus container CPU throttling, to separate broker-side slowness from client retry inflation before any further restart.

Recommend adding a readiness probe to the kafka container so the pod is not Ready before Kafka Server starts, and consider persistent storage for /tmp/kafka-logs so a pod replacement does not discard broker state.
Review whether the 14:21:34 rollout restart of Deployment kafka was scheduled and whether restarting it under load on the checkout path is acceptable.
Verify downstream and customer impact separately, for example whether orders that received a 504 at the proxy were later completed, before claiming any business consequence.
